title: Per-route observability overhaul for embeddings + rerank pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Modernize telemetry for embeddings + rerank endpoints to provide per-route dashboards, end-to-end tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns. This ticket covers instrumentation changes, metrics & tag schema, aggregation pipelines, dashboards, and alerting rules so product and SRE teams can detect quality regressions, latency spikes, and cost anomalies per customer route. The goal is measurable SLOs and actionable alerts with minimal runtime overhead.
background: Current observability for embeddings and rerank is coarse-grained: stackdriver metrics aggregate across many routes and do not capture route_id, batch size, model variant, or kv-cache hit rates. This makes it hard to: (1) attribute cost to customers/routes, (2) correlate quality regressions to model changes, and (3) debug high-latency tails that only affect certain request patterns. Several customer incidents in Q1 indicated missing per-route visibility for rerank regressions and billing surprises from unseen batch amplification.
goals: Emit route-scoped metrics and spans from request ingress through embedding model and reranker execution
Provide Grafana dashboards with latency heatmaps, p50/p95/p99, cost-per-request, and quality metrics (ndcg@10, recall@k) per route
Add alerts for combined signals: quality drop + increased latency or cost per request
Ensure telemetry has bounded overhead (target < 3% CPU/net) and respects PII/PIA guidelines
Support rollbacks and gradual rollout with runtime flagging
non_goals: Implement new billing pipelines for invoices (handled by billing team separately)
Change underlying rerank model architectures as part of this ticket
acceptance_criteria: All embeddings and rerank HTTP/gRPC handlers include route_id and route_metadata as span attributes for 100% of requests in sampled traces
Metrics: per-route histogram of request latency, per-route counter for requests, per-route gauge for avg_tokens_per_embedding, per-route cost estimate metric (model*tokens*batch_factor)

Dashboards: a per-route default dashboard template rendered in Grafana with latency percentiles, success/error rates, cost breakdown by model and batch, KV cache hit rate, and recent quality evaluation (ndcg@10 sample)
Alerting: at least three alert rules exist and are documented: (1) latency SLO burn rate per route, (2) ndcg@10 drop > 5% relative to baseline, (3) cost-per-request deviance > 30% over 24h
Instrumentation rollout has a canary in prod with 5% traffic and automated rollback if trace ingestion error rate > 0.5%
Telemetry overhead validated under synthetic load (1000 r/s) and does not increase p50 latency by more than 10ms or CPU by more than 3%
Privacy: no raw user content is emitted in spans or metrics; PII scrubber applied before adding any request fields to telemetry
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Instrumentation: add route_id, route_version, batch_size, model_variant, tokens_requested, kv_cache_hit to spans and metrics. Add sampling logic for token-level traces (1 in 10000 full payload traces)
Phase 2 - Aggregation/Backfill: extend metrics ingestion pipeline to accept new label sets, update Prometheus/metrics schemas, and backfill 7-day baselines for initial routes
Phase 3 - Dashboards: produce Grafana per-route dashboard template and onboarding docs for PMs/CS to enable for customers
Phase 4 - Alerts & SLOs: define SLOs per route and implement alert rules in Alertmanager with runbook links
Phase 5 - Rollout: canary (5%), ramp to 25%, full rollout with monitoring for ingestion errors and resource utilization
Phase 6 - Quality integration: wire sampled evals (synthetic prompt sets) to dashboards and provide drift trend lines
risks_and_mitigation: High cardinality label explosion: mitigate by using conservative label set and allowing sampled route aggregation; use hashed route_id in high-cardinality shards
Telemetry cost increase: cap trace full-payload sampling, compress and TTL metrics with downsampling after 7d
Privacy leak: enforce scrubber and QA review; security review required before ramp
Runtime overhead causing latency regressions: bench locally and in perf test cluster; enable runtime flag to disable heavy telemetry per node
dashboard_widgets: Cost breakdown bar: model + quantization + batching contribution
Quality trend: ndcg@10 and recall@k sampled daily
Top-10 routes by cost and by latency regression
alerts: Latency SLO burn rate > 4 for 10m for a single route
ndcg@10 drop > 5% relative to 7-day baseline for a route
Estimated cost per request > 30% above baseline for 24h
privacy_and_compliance: All telemetry fields must be reviewed by Security and Product Compliance
No raw prompt or user PII leaves the service — scrub before emission
Support opt-out for customers who do not want per-route retention beyond 7 days
rollout_plan: Create feature flag `observability_per_route_v2` in config service
Enable flag for internal routes and staging for 48h
Canary: enable for 5% production traffic for 72h and verify dashboards/ingestion
Ramp to 25% for 48h, then to 100% if no ingestion issues
Coordinate with Billing and CS for enabling per-customer dashboards
